extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers for ACL 2023 (program committee, area reviewers of an NLP conference)
extracted.subtask_description: Complete a full peer review for an ACL 2023 submission, including mandatory written review, numeric scores for soundness/excitement/reproducibility/confidence, ethical/anonymity judgments, and confidential comments for chairs. The form is specific to ACL conference review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paper summary and contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: What is this paper about and what contributions does it make? Please describe what problem or question this paper addresses, and the main contributions that it makes towards a solution or answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following kinds of contributions are all welcome at ACL: computationally-aided linguistic analysis, NLP engineering experiment, reproduction study, new data resources (particularly for low-resource languages), approaches for data- and compute efficiency, position papers, surveys, publicly available software and pre-trained models. Describe problem, main contributions, and how they advance the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to accept
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the strengths of this paper and what would be the main benefits to the NLP community if this paper were to be presented at the conference or accepted into Findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List the paper's strengths and expected benefits to the community. Be explicit about concrete impacts (e.g., new dataset, improved method, novel analysis). Follow the conference policies on what should not be considered weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: What are the weaknesses of this paper and what would be the main risks of having this paper presented at the conference (other than lack of space to present better papers) or accepted into Findings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List substantive weaknesses and risks of acceptance (technical flaws, unsupported claims, methodological problems, ethical risks). Reviewers must be sure to follow conference policies on what should not be considered weaknesses (e.g., minor formatting or anonymization issues).

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions for the Author(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions for the Author(s) that you would like answers for in the author response, particularly those relevant for your overall recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer letters (A, B, C) for questions since reviewers will have numbers; label questions to ease discussion (e.g., Question 2C). Some common questions are covered in the Responsible NLP Checklist—check the authors' answers first.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing References
rubrics_metrics.description: List any references that should be included in the bibliography or need to be discussed in more depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you believe the work is not novel or misses prior work, give full citations. Note: contemporaneous work (in the three months before the deadline) is not required to be cited and should not be held against authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typos, Grammar, Style, and Presentation Improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Typographical or grammatical errors, stylistic issues, and suggestions to improve organization, motivation, or explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List typos/grammar errors and stylistic issues with line numbers for easy reference. Also note parts that are difficult to follow and suggest concrete reorganization or clearer explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation — Soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Should this paper be accepted to any of the venues associated with ACL 2023? Focus on how sound and thorough this study is, not novelty/excitement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the paper clearly states scientific claims and provides adequate support. For experimental papers: depth/breadth of research questions, technical soundness of experiments, methodological validity of evaluation. For position papers/surveys: whether the current state is represented and counter-arguments acknowledged. For resource papers: data collection methodology and differences from existing resources described in sufficient detail. Adjust baseline to an average ACL paper of the given type (long vs short). Use these score definitions: 5=Excellent (one of the most thorough I've seen given its type), 4=Strong (sufficient support for claims; extra experiments not essential), 3=Good (sufficient support for major claims; some minor points need details), 2=Borderline (main claims not sufficiently supported; major technical/methodological problems), 1=Poor (not sufficiently thorough or not relevant to ACL). If paper is not relevant to ACL, select 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation — Excitement (Long paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: How excited/enthusiastic are you for this long paper to be accepted to ACL 2023? Focus on novelty, personal interest, and perceived potential impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excitement is subjective; possible sources: novelty (conceptual breakthroughs, corrections, negative results), personal interest/usefulness, or potential impact (lowering barriers, enabling new applications). Adjust baseline for long papers. Score definitions: 5=Transformative (likely to change subfield; candidate for best paper), 4.5=Exciting (changed my thinking; would fight for acceptance), 4=Strong (deepens understanding or lowers barriers), 3.5=Leaning positive, 3=Ambivalent (merits but key weaknesses), 2.5=Leaning negative, 2=Mediocre (marginal contributions), 1.5=Weak, 1=Poor (cannot identify contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Recommendation — Excitement (Short paper)
rubrics_metrics.description: How excited/enthusiastic are you for this short paper to be accepted? Adjust baseline for short-paper expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short papers are not expected to be big conceptual breakthroughs but can be novel/impactful (e.g., core resource, well-argued counter-perspective, significant negative result). Use same qualitative score labels as long-paper excitement (5 Transformative ... 1 Poor) but judged against short paper norms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer Confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: How confident are you in your assessment of this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 5 = Positive (read carefully; very familiar with related work), 4 = Quite sure (checked important points), 3 = Pretty sure (may have missed details; didn't carefully check math/experimental design), 2 = Willing to defend but fairly likely missed details, 1 = Not my area or paper was hard to understand (evaluation is an educated guess).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for Best Paper Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think this paper should be considered for a Best Paper Award? (Separate awards for long/short; also Outstanding Paper Awards.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes/No. Provide brief justification for award recommendation. Comments will not be shared with authors but may be made public (anonymous) if the paper receives an award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: How do you rate the paper's reproducibility? Will members of the ACL community be able to reproduce or verify the results in this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 5 = Could easily reproduce the results; 4 = Could mostly reproduce but some variation due to sample variance or minor protocol interpretation; 3 = Could reproduce with some difficulty (underspecified parameters, unavailable data); 2 = Would be hard (data not available outside author's institution/consortium; insufficient details); 1 = Could not reproduce the results no matter how hard they tried. N/A = Doesn’t apply (paper has no empirical results).

rubrics_metrics.name: Checklist feedback (Responsible NLP Checklist usefulness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the authors’ answers to the Responsible NLP Checklist useful for evaluating the submission?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This question is about collecting feedback on the usefulness of the checklist itself; it is not an evaluation of the paper. Indicate whether the checklist answers helped your evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns — Send for in-depth ethics review?
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent of quality, should this paper be sent for an in-depth ethics review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No/Yes. Review relevant Ethics review questions and Ethics FAQ as needed. If you think the paper needs special ethics scrutiny, explain why; ACL has a small ethics committee for challenging cases and will try to provide a separate review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you know the identity of some authors of this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale: 5 = Yes, I have seen a non-anonymized version posted online after Dec 20, 2022 (may be an anonymity violation), 4 = Yes, seen non-anonymized version on or before Dec 20, 2022, 3 = Yes, I know identities via other means (e.g., senior area chair), 2 = Not sure but have a good guess, 1 = No (do not know authors). Note: only option 5 may be in violation of anonymity policy. If 3, 4, or 5 chosen, provide details (e.g., URL). Provide a detailed review regardless.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Response — Read?
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the author response (rebuttal)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes used for committee-only field: 4 = N/A (before rebuttal period), 3 = N/A (authors did not provide response), 2 = Yes (I have read the response), 1 = No (I have not read the response). This answer is shared with committee only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Update — Changes after rebuttal/discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: After reading the author response and discussing with other reviewers, have you changed your scores?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Codes (committee-only): 6 = N/A (before rebuttal), 5 = N/A (authors did not provide response), 4 = Yes, response/discussion changed my mind on ‘soundness’, 3 = Yes, changed my mind on ‘excitement’, 2 = Yes, changed my mind on both, 1 = No, I didn’t change my mind. Note: reviewers were provided a clarification about score meanings—if you changed scores due to reinterpretation rather than response/discussion, choose “No, I didn’t change my mind.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation for Media Dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you think the paper might have particular public interest and should be considered for lay summaries for journalists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yes/No. If Yes, provide a brief public interest justification describing why (e.g., broad societal impact, topical relevance). This information is shared with committee only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Comments to the Area Chair and Peer Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information you want to share with the area chair and other reviewers assigned to this paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this field for strong opinions that may offend authors or anything that could expose reviewer identity to authors. These comments are shared only with area chair and co-reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Comments to Senior Area Chairs and PC Chairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential information you want to say to Senior Area Chairs and PCs only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use for matters that should not be visible to other reviewers or the area chair; shared only with senior area chairs and program chairs.
